title: Magnetic Properties of High-Entropy Alloy FeCoNiTi

recollection.starting_material: Elemental Fe, Co, Ni, and Ti powders (nominal equiatomic composition)
recollection.intervention: Mechanical alloying followed by arc melting and homogenization anneal
recollection.structure: Primarily a single-phase body-centered cubic (BCC) high-entropy alloy with minor Ti-rich secondary phases
recollection.mechanism: Magnetic moments of Fe, Co, and Ni aligned in the BCC lattice; Ti dilutes exchange interactions but stabilizes the single phase
recollection.results: Saturation magnetization ~1.1–1.3 T at room temperature, coercivity ~30–70 Oe, Curie temperature ~600–650 K (best guess)

score.note: The recollection is substantially incorrect. It invents mechanical alloying and homogenization, misidentifies the fcc+C14 dual-phase structure as BCC, gives an incompatible magnetic mechanism, and reports values far from the observed transitions (1084, 214, and 168 K) and coercivity (667 Oe at 400 K).
